messages:
sophia_oncall: node pool us-west-2-gpu-4 reported a cascade of container crashes ~23:04 UTC, starting with OOMs then immediate task restarts. seeing CUDA illegal memory access in runtime logs. creating thread.
incident-bot: incident created: INC-2026-142; priority P1; assignees: @sophia_oncall, @kai_runtime.
sophia_oncall: summary log (tail):
```
[2026-03-15T23:03:58Z] runtime: serve: request id=abc123 token_len=512
[2026-03-15T23:04:01Z] runtime: nvml: device 0: GPU panic
[2026-03-15T23:04:01Z] runtime: err: CUDA: illegal memory access (misaligned device address) at kernel.cu:342
[2026-03-15T23:04:02Z] containerd: process exited code=139
```

kai_runtime: looking at kernel traces now. early signs point to an intermittent pagewalk misalignment when SMMU updates coincide with eviction. not a model regression.
mike_sre: current scope: 6 nodes in us-west-2 pool flapped, ~1200 requests failed with 5xx in last 10m. autoscaling partially triggered but new nodes also hit same condition.
jen_support: support queue: 3 customers reported latency spikes and partial request failures (id 0x7b9f), one customer hitting 25% error rate on embeddings. flagging for potential SLA impact.
adrian_prodeng: any quick mitigations? pref rollback or node cordon?
sophia_oncall: immediate plan: cordon affected nodes, drain replicas to warm nodes in other AZs, enable fallback to quantized-small model variant for new requests, and disable batch-unification that increases gpu memory pressure.
kai_runtime: runbook commands:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-74.usw2
kubectl drain gpu-node-74.usw2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# scale down pool to avoid scheduling new pods there
gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize ig-gpu-usw2 --size=0
```

(doing cordon+drain now)
ops-bot: cordon initiated on 3 nodes, drain started.
sophia_oncall: note: do NOT do a global rollout rollback yet — we need to ensure fallback removes the pathological memory pattern.
kai_runtime: quick patch candidate: disable async page prefetch in serving runtime v2.3.1 on canaries (affects KV-pagewalk path). patch applied to canary group (2 nodes) — monitoring.
adrian_prodeng: can we route traffic away from canary if things degrade? set canary weight 0.2 -> 0.05.
mike_sre: telemetry: error spike reduced from 18%->6% on canary after disabling prefetch. memory OOMs drop on canary nodes. looks promising.
jen_support: notifying impacted customers with initial blurb: "We're investigating GPU runtime crashes causing elevated error rates; we're applying mitigations and will update within 30 minutes." posting now. :loudspeaker: 
sophia_oncall: next: for affected nodes, collect full coredumps and nvcrash logs. commands:
```
/var/log/containers/*runtime*.log > /tmp/runtime-tail.log
sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -n 500 > /tmp/nv-persist.log
sudo cp /var/crash/*.dmp /tmp/collect/
```

kai_runtime: grabbed a reproducible stack trace from one coredump: kernel pointer write to unaligned address in cuLaunchKernel path — likely a timing window with SMMU TLB invalidation during kernel launch. attaching snippet:
```
#0 0x7f3ab12c in cuLaunchKernel+0x4f
#1 0x7f3b01da in runtimeLaunchKernel+0x1a2
#2 0x7f3b0321 in serveForward+0x88
```

mike_sre: hooking an emergency firewall: temporarily throttle large batch requests to reduce concurrent kernels per device. applied via rate-limiter rad-limiter config.
adrian_prodeng: estimate of customer impact? jen_support?
jen_support: current list: cust-A (high-traffic embeddings), cust-D (real-time chat), cust-F (internal infra tests). cust-A and cust-D see 10-30% error bursts; cust-F saw intermittent flakiness. We sent initial message and will update when canary shows full resolution.
sophia_oncall: timeline: 23:03 initial failures, 23:14 canary patch applied, 23:22 canary error rate dropped; 23:30 starting staged rollout to remaining pool with patch and reduced batch sizes.
incident-bot: rolling update started: rollout_id=rl-4550009876-1 target=us-west-2-gpu-pool step=staged
kai_runtime: small gotcha: one older kernel driver (470.x) still present on a node; it didn't respect SMMU ordering fix. skipping that node from rollout. marking for repro/upgrade later.
mike_sre: observation: when we drained and re-scheduled, pods scheduled onto smaller-instance sandbox nodes didn't reproduce — suggests interplay between device firmware + instance type.
ads (adrian_prodeng): request to product: consider adding runtime config to force single-kernel-per-device for fragile kernels as a long-term safety. filing RFC.
sophia_oncall: customer update draft: "We identified a GPU driver/kernel interaction causing illegal device memory accesses under high eviction/paging conditions. We've applied a runtime mitigation that reduces batch-induced concurrency and disables async prefetch, which reduced errors on canaries. We're performing staged rollout; some customers may still see intermittent errors while we complete remediation. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary including root cause and mitigations." approve?
jen_support: approve, minor edits sent.
ops-bot: rollout step 2: 40% completed in 23:40 UTC; no new OOMs in updated nodes.
kai_runtime: collecting follow-up artifacts: device traces, SMMU pagewalk logs, driver nv-host logs, and runtime internal memstats. storing in /mnt/incident-logs/INC-2026-142/
adrian_prodeng: action items assigned:
- kai_runtime: reproduce in lab with same kernel/firmware combo (ETA 24h)
- mike_sre: add throttling rule + rollback playbook (ETA 2h)
- sophia_oncall & jen_support: finalize customer comms and SLA impact table (ETA 1h)
- adrian_prodeng: RFC for single-kernel safety flag (ETA 2d)
sophia_oncall: closing loop for now — we're holding on a full rollback. if error rates on rollout exceed 10% for any 5m window -> immediate rollback to previous runtime config.
jen_support: posted update to customers: "Mitigation is in progress; error rates dropping on updated hosts; ETA next update 30m."
incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> partial, P1 -> monitoring.
mike_sre: note for postmortem: check host firmware versions vs driver, and whether cloud provider recently pushed microcode updates to those instance types.
kai_runtime: will attach kernel/dmesg snippets to the incident file. last log shows repeating: "gpu0: pagewalk: invalid alignment at va=0x7ffd123400" — correlates with device eviction windows.
sophia_oncall: thanks team. keep this thread active for handoffs. I'll remain on until full rollout complete. :thumbsup:
jen_support: moving tickets to "incident - in progress" and linking to this thread.
(23:50) sophia_oncall: full rollout now at 100% on patched runtime; monitoring. final verification window set to 30m.
(00:22) mike_sre: verification window passed; no new device illegal access reports. marking incident as resolved -> postmortem to follow.
(00:30) kai_runtime: uploaded reproducer script and lab notes to internal repo: repo.redwood/inference/issue-INC-2026-142; include driver/firmware matrix.
(01:05) adrian_prodeng: scheduled follow-up postmortem meeting tomorrow 15:00 UTC.
(01:10) sophia_oncall: closing comments: thanks everyone for quick triage. root cause suspected: race between SMMU invalidation and kernel launch under heavy eviction; mitigation: runtime disables async prefetch and reduces concurrent kernels per GPU. long-term: driver/firmware alignment + single-kernel safety flag.
incident-bot: incident closed as "resolved" after verification window. artifacts stored at /mnt/incident-logs/INC-2026-142/complete.tar.gz
